prerequisites: Achievement of the second study section, with at least 42 ECTS points from the first study section.
Mastery of common software development tools: IDE with editor, compiler, debugger.
Solid knowledge in programming languages such as Java, Python, PHP, JavaScript, Go.

learning_outcomes.text: The students are able to practically apply at least one specific project management method (preferably Scrum or Kanban).
The students are able to use concrete tools that are typically employed in the context of an IT project (IDE, RCS, ticket system, Scrum Board).
The students are able to deal with technical and non-technical problems that may arise during the execution of a multi-week project.
The students are able to analyze a complex technical task and successfully complete it in a team over a semester.
The students are able to report on project progress in oral and/or written form, with varying but always appropriate detail.
The students are able to recognize business aspects of a project in addition to technical problems and support them appropriately to ensure overall success.

syllabus_topics: Practical application of a project management method (e.g., Scrum, Kanban)
Planning of tasks and effort estimation in a team
Practical application of software development tools (IDE, RCS, Ticket System, Scrum Board)
Application of agile software development techniques: Pair Programming, Test Driven Development, Unit Testing, CI/CD
Reporting of project progress, e.g., Daily Scrum

assessment_methods.method: Individual contribution to the common task
Project report (1500 to 7500 words or 5 to 25 pages)
Oral presentation of results (15 to 45 minutes)

assessment_rules: The project work is a group effort where several students collaborate on a common task. Each student must contribute individually, submit a project report (1500-7500 words or approx. 5-25 pages), and, if applicable, present the results orally (15-45 minutes). The lecturer will communicate expectations regarding deadlines, format, and proof of individual performance, as well as criteria for assessment/grading, at the beginning of the project.
